claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on high-entropy-alloy thermal-conductivity data can accurately identify alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The relevant input material space includes high-entropy alloys with varying compositions and microstructures.
The model is trained using high-entropy alloys with known thermal-conductivity properties.
The predictive approach applies to thermal-insulation operation from 300 K to 1000 K.
Grain-boundary scattering is a mechanism affecting phonon thermal conductivity in the relevant high-entropy alloys.
Point-defect scattering is a mechanism affecting phonon thermal conductivity in the relevant high-entropy alloys.
Patterns and correlations learned from the dataset encode relationships to phonon-scattering mechanisms.
Learning correlations related to phonon scattering enables accurate prediction of thermal conductivity.
The model will predict thermal conductivity with less than 10% error relative to experimental values.
The model will outperform current traditional thermal-conductivity predictions by at least 20%.
Applicability is limited to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and microstructures resemble those represented in the training data.
Prediction accuracy may depend on training-dataset quality and size.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the machine-learning algorithm and model parameters.
Experimental thermal-conductivity values differing from predictions by more than 15% would falsify the hypothesis.
